evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'you have about five or ten minutes to go over that information' but does not use the standard framing of '10 to 15 minutes' + 'quote you can depend on' + wait for yes. The time estimate is non-standard and no explicit promise of a dependable quote or wait for confirmation is present.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked as 'do you have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call besides pricing' — this comes before logistics probing (property type, square footage) begins, so technically asked before probing, but customer answers 'No' so no concerns are raised.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer raised no concerns in Section 2, so no follow-up was required.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — customer raised no concerns, so no reflection was needed.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type: 'house but it's been inverted into a duplex'; floor info: 'three or four steps up to the first floor'; parking: driveway discussed; destination: 'above garage apartment that has some stairs and the stairs make a right angle'; square footage: 1200 sq ft origin, 800 sq ft destination; room count: 'one bedroom and an office' at origin, 'just one bedroom' at destination; downsizing confirmed: 'we will take everything some stuff will go into the apartment. Some and a few things will go into the garage.'
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. Rep discusses hourly rate and what is included but does not ask 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not asked. No reference to typical box count or overflow check for items like china or book collections.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep states 'for a typical move the size takes two movers between three and a half to five and a half hours' and then personalizes: 'since you are moving to a smaller space with a short drive I would estimate that it taking two movers one truck between three and a half and four and a half hours' and gives budget range '$672 and $864'. Also anchors to customer's prior experience: 'You remember how long it took them to move you into the house that you're in' and uses that to refine estimate to 'three and a half, probably four hours.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Hourly rate stated ($192 for two movers and 126-foot truck). Included items listed: 'fuel and truck taxes, insurance... wrap pads... tools for reassembly.' 2.5-hour minimum mentioned: 'two and a half hour minimum, and then once we go over that minimum the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments.' No explicit trip fee, overnight fee, or 'not a guess' framing, but the core pricing transparency and time-commitment language is present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moves directly from estimate into booking: 'there's no deposit required to get on the schedule. I do have that 8:39 AM arrival and then I do have the 12:30 to 230 arrival time. Would you like us to help you with your that move on Monday the nineteenth?' No pause for customer to react to the price before moving to the close.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Delivered: 'we have our on time guarantee we value your time. So, if we can't make it in the window we arrange, we mainly start discounting money of your final bill.' The discount-for-lateness terms are present, though 'mainly' is slightly vague on immediacy.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Not delivered. Rep does not mention the No Worries Damage Coverage, the $2,000 limit, the no-deductible framing, or that it is built into the rate.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep does not ask a version of 'Does that put those to rest?' There are no unresolved concerns to close anyway (customer said 'No' in Section 2), so this is technically a skip-condition, but the explicit close-the-loop language is not present.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks 'If you wouldn't mind just going over that confirmation email checking the bullet items to make sure I didn't make any mistakes and then do you have any other questions for me?' This is functionally equivalent to 'any other questions?' — a throwaway close, not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' language.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' is present.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Asked plainly: 'Would you like us to help you with your that move on Monday the nineteenth?' No easy-out softening detected ('or I can just email this over').
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No statement that the rate is locked in or guaranteed at the quoted price.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms arrival window ('8:30 AM to 9:00 AM arrival'), date ('Monday the nineteenth'), and contact number (verified earlier, 713-501-3992). Missing: explicit confirmation of crew size (assumed two, but not restated), destination address (assumed but not repeated in confirmation), and notes left for crew about customer concerns (stair pivot situation was discussed but no note-to-crew language used). Email confirmation is offered: 'I have you scheduled on there, if you do have any questions or concerns don't hesitate to reach out' and 'if you wouldn't mind just going over that confirmation email checking the bullet items.'

top_strength: Excellent logistics discovery — Brianne thoroughly probed the property details (duplex setup, stair angles, parking constraints, square footage, downsizing), and she personalized the estimate using the customer's prior move experience to refine her time prediction.
coaching_note: Never skip 'Does that feel fair?' — this call went straight from pricing to the close without letting the customer react to the estimate, and the No Worries Damage Coverage was completely omitted (a missing Two Promise).
